generation.promptText: Locked camera, one continuous six-second shot. Preserve the exact woman, clothes, green studio and black shoe. Her anatomical LEFT hand is on screen RIGHT and handles the card throughout. Draw ONE magenta card just clear of the shoe outlet, then immediately sweep it low diagonally toward the empty lower-RIGHT landing spot shown in the last image. The entire dealing action stays beside and in front of the shoe, on the RIGHT side of her body. While traveling outward, her left thumb and fingertips roll the card over exactly ONCE through an edge-on position: the original upper physical face ends DOWN, the original underside ends UP. This is a real 180-degree turnover, not a flat spin. Without stopping to show it, lower that same card flat at the new lower-right position, release it by 3.5 seconds, then return the empty left hand to the original shoe-ready pose by 5.3 seconds and settle. The new card stays on the table. The existing centre card stays untouched. No travel toward the centre card, no hand transfer, no display pause, no second turnover. Natural following gaze and subtle right-hand movement are allowed. Both card faces are plain magenta tracking surfaces, no print. Keep fingertip contact until release; preserve a thin rigid card, all fingers, body scale and camera framing. End with the same body, hand and gaze anchor as the first image, plus one new card on the table and the next card ready in the shoe.
